pillars.label: Evidence
pillars.help: Is the link between this gene and lupus real, causal, and current?

pillars.label: Tractability
pillars.help: Could a drug molecule actually engage this protein?

pillars.label: Safety
pillars.help: Is inhibiting it likely to be tolerated? Higher is safer.

pillars.label: Opportunity
pillars.help: Is the space still open, and has the pharmacology been proven nearby?

criteria.label: Genetic association
criteria.help: Variant-level human genetics tying the gene to SLE — the evidence class that best predicts clinical success.

criteria.label: Overall SLE association
criteria.help: Open Targets' combined association score across every evidence class.

criteria.label: Literature specificity
criteria.help: Share of the gene's entire PubMed footprint that is lupus literature. Separates genes the field studies in lupus from genes studied everywhere.

criteria.label: Research momentum
criteria.help: Papers in the last 5 years against the 5 before — is interest accelerating right now?

criteria.label: Best modality
criteria.help: The most advanced tractability assessment across small molecule, antibody, degrader and other modalities.

criteria.label: Chemical matter
criteria.help: Known ligands, a bindable pocket, small-molecule binders, high-quality chemical probes — whether you would be starting from zero.

criteria.label: Biologic accessibility
criteria.help: Secreted or membrane-embedded, so an antibody can reach it. The modality that has actually worked in lupus.

criteria.label: Family precedent
criteria.help: How often drugs have succeeded against this protein class historically.

criteria.label: LoF tolerance
criteria.help: gnomAD constraint. Humans carrying loss-of-function variants without harm is a natural experiment in what inhibiting the target does.

criteria.label: Mouse knockout burden
criteria.help: How many significant phenotypes the mouse knockout shows. Fewer means fewer surprises on-target.

criteria.label: Non-essentiality
criteria.help: Cell-line essentiality. A common-essential gene is a bad target for systemic inhibition.

criteria.label: Expression focus
criteria.help: Restricted to a few tissues and cell types rather than ubiquitous — fewer places to cause off-tissue effects.

criteria.label: Clean safety record
criteria.help: Absence of curated adverse-event liabilities and cancer-driver status for this target.

criteria.label: Unclaimed space
criteria.help: Runs backwards to the leaderboard: no SLE programme scores high, an approved SLE drug scores near zero. That target is answered, not open.

criteria.label: Cross-indication precedent
criteria.help: A drug already hitting this target in another immune-mediated disease — proven human pharmacology one indication away.

criteria.label: Network proximity
criteria.help: Physical interaction with proteins that already carry an SLE programme at Phase 2 or beyond — guilt by association with validated biology.
